thumb.title: PV Sindhu is back in the top 5

concept: A comeback told as a climb. The hero puts where she was, 'No. 11 in October', in muted grey and the news, 'Sindhu is back in the top 5', in white, so the jump is the first thing you read. Slide 2 answers why with one giant 19, the months she went without a title before the Japan Open in July, because the drought is what makes the climb matter. Slide 3 is a four-step timeline of the results that moved her up, and slide 4 points to the World Tour Finals in Hangzhou with a question for fans. Indian-sports orange, rings that draw themselves behind the text in the reel, type only: no player photos and no BWF or tournament logos.
caption:
World No. 11 six weeks ago. World No. 5 today.

PV Sindhu is back in the women's singles top 5 of the BWF world rankings for the first time since November 2022. She is 31.

Why now: in July she ended a 19-month title drought at the Japan Open, a Super 750, beating four-time winner Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-17 in the final. She then finished runner-up at the French Open and won the Hylo Open on November 1.

What's next: she has qualified for the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou from December 9 to 13.

Can Sindhu win in Hangzhou? Tell us below.
